General
Expand All
Can you tell me my chances of acceptance or pre-screen my application before formally applying?
We evaluate candidates holistically based on all application components (transcripts, essays, resume, etc.) and cannot provide a preliminary assessment or determine chances of admission prior to receiving a full application. However, if you have specific questions about program fit or are seeking advice about strengthening your application, please feel free to contact us.
Can an applicant apply to more than one program at a time?
We recommend applying to one program per application cycle. Please carefully review each program’s focus and skill development. If you have questions about program fit to achieve your career goals, please contact your admissions advisor.
Do I have to have an undergraduate major in the same area as the graduate program in which I wish to study?
Not necessarily. Many of our graduate programs welcome applicants from a wide variety of academic backgrounds. While a direct major is not always required, some programs may expect specific prerequisite coursework, foundational skills, or relevant experience prior to enrollment.
We encourage you to review the specific admissions requirements for your program of interest to see if any prerequisite courses or background knowledge are needed before applying.
Can I transfer credits from another institution?
Credit transfer policies vary by school and academic program. In some cases, students who have completed relevant graduate-level coursework may be eligible to transfer credits or seek an exemption/waiver for specific core courses allowing them to replace those requirements with advanced electives.
How long does it take to receive an admissions decision?
Decision timelines vary by program and application cycle, but most applicants can expect to receive an admissions decision within 4 to 6 weeks after submitting a complete application, including all required supporting documents and letters of recommendation.
Once a decision has been rendered, you will receive an email notification instructing you to log in to your applicant portal to view your official decision letter.
What career services and professional development support are available to graduate students?
Brandeis provides comprehensive career support tailored to graduate students across all academic stages. Students can access personalized 1-on-1 career advising, CV/résumé tailoring and interview preparation. The university also offers regular workshops and seminars covering career transitions, networking strategies and professional skill-building. Additionally, students can tap into robust networking and mentorship opportunities with alumni and industry professionals, as well as full access to digital platforms like Handshake for job listings and Big Interview for mock interview prep.
What are the highest-ranked graduate programs at Brandeis University?
As an R1 research university, Brandeis consistently earns top national and international rankings across social policy, health policy, business and the humanities.
Brandeis University’s graduate programs consistently perform well across national and international rankings, particularly in social policy, health policy, business and humanities research. Brandeis is an R1 research institution listed among top private value universities and research institutions by Forbes, Kiplinger’s and U.S. News & World Report.
U.S. News & World Report ranks the Heller School for Social Policy and Management #11 nationwide for health policy and management and #15 for social policy. Heller also places in the top 20% of all graduate schools of public affairs in the United States.
The School of Business and Economics is an AACSB accredited institution with programs ranked among the best business schools in the United States by U.S. News & World Report and The Economist and Financial Times, with notable top-tier marks in educational experience, faculty diversity and international diversity.
The MBA program ranked #10 for Best MBA for Nonprofit (Princeton Review) and #57 globally (QS World University Rankings).
The Master of Science in Finance (MSF) program ranked #7 in the U.S. by Financial Times and #6 by TFE Times.
The Master of Science in Business Analytics (MSBA) program ranked #5 nationwide by TFE Times.
If admitted, can I defer my admission?
Admitted students may request to defer their enrollment for up to one year. Deferrals are reviewed on a case-by-case basis. To submit a request, you must first pay your enrollment deposit. Please note that financial aid and scholarship awards may be subject to re-evaluation for the deferred term. Contact the admissions team for more information about the deferral process.
Application
Expand All
What are the requirements for admission?
Requirements vary by program, but all applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) prior to matriculation.
Standard application components include an online application and application fee, statement of purpose, resume/CV, unofficial transcripts and recommender contact details (for automated letter submission). Depending on your program, you may also need to submit standardized test scores, a writing sample or participate in an interview. Please check the application requirements pages for specific requirements and deadlines.
When are the application deadlines for graduate programs?
Application deadlines vary by program and entry term. For specific deadlines, visit the page for the program you're interested in or the How to Apply page.
What is the application fee?
The online application fee is $75. This fee is required for all applicants unless you are eligible for an application fee waiver.
Who is eligible for an application fee waiver?
Visit the Application Fee Waivers page to see if you are eligible for a fee waiver.
Are there prerequisites for admission?
Certain programs have prerequisites for admission. Please visit the application requirements pages to learn more about prerequisites.
Is a GRE/GMAT required for admission?
Standardized test scores are optional for most of our master’s programs, unless specifically required by your program of interest. While a GMAT or GRE score is not required for admission, submitting strong scores can be a great way to demonstrate your quantitative aptitude and strengthen your overall application.
Can I apply before completing my bachelor's degree?
Yes. You are welcome to apply during your final year of undergraduate study. You can submit unofficial transcripts displaying your coursework completed to date as part of your application.
If admitted, your offer of admission will be contingent upon successfully earning your bachelor’s degree (or international equivalent) prior to matriculation. Once you graduate, you must provide official, final transcripts verifying degree conferral before starting your graduate studies.
I have a three year bachelor’s degree. Am I eligible to apply?
Yes. Applicants who hold a three-year bachelor's degree from an accredited international institution are eligible to apply. To be considered, your degree must be deemed equivalent to a U.S. four-year bachelor's degree.
Depending on the country or system in which your degree was conferred, the admissions office may request a credential evaluation service review of your coursework, total credits and institutional accreditation to confirm equivalency.
Transcripts
Expand All
Am I required to submit transcripts with my application?
Applicants are required to submit transcripts from any college or university where they earned or will earn a degree, or where they completed 12 or more credits that do not appear as grades courses on another transcript they are submitting.
For additional information, please review the application requirements pages.
Can I apply with an unofficial transcript, or is an official transcript required?
Unofficial transcripts are accepted for application review. Official transcripts are only required upon enrollment.
Do I need to provide an evaluation of my studies in addition to my transcript(s)?
Transcript evaluations are typically not required, however, Brandeis does reserve the right to require transcript evaluations at any time during the admission process. If a transcript evaluation is necessary, we will contact you directly and you will be asked to provide a course-by-course evaluation from an accredited evaluation company that currently holds membership to the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES).
Should I submit transcripts for my study abroad program, transfer coursework, non-degree programs or certificates?
If your study abroad courses, transfer coursework and grades appear on your primary degree-granting institution's transcript, a separate transcript is generally not required. If they do not appear with individual grades, you must submit an official transcript from the study abroad institution. We do not require submission of transcripts for non-degree programs or certificates.
Letters of Recommendation
Expand All
How many letters of recommendation do I need?
The required number of letters of recommendation varies among programs. Please visit our application requirements pages to see specific requirements by program.
How are letters of recommendation submitted?
Recommendation letters must be submitted electronically through the online application portal. Please provide an official institutional or corporate email address (e.g., @university.edu or @company.com) for each recommender. Submissions from personal email domains (such as Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo or 163) are strongly discouraged and may require additional verification by the admissions committee.
Should I submit a professional or academic letter of recommendation?
We accept both professional recommendations (from supervisors, clients, colleagues or mentors) and academic recommendations (from professors or academic advisors). If you have 2+ years of full-time work experience, a professional letter is strongly encouraged.
Can I submit my application before my letters of recommendation are received?
Yes. You are welcome to submit your application prior to receiving your letters of recommendation. Your application will be held for review until all required materials, including recommendation letters, are received.
My recommender is not receiving the email instructions to upload their letter. What should I do?
If your recommender hasn’t received our automated email, please ask your recommender to check their spam, junk or promotional folders as email filters occasionally misroute automated messages. If applicable, please ask them to ensure their security software or email server is set to accept emails from our domain.
Alternatively, you are welcome to have your recommender email their letter as a PDF or Doc attachment to gradadmissions@brandeis.edu. The email will need to be sent from their professional email address as listed on your application. Our office will then attach the letter to your application.
Can I change or update my recommender's email address after submitting my application?
Yes. You can edit or update your recommender’s email address through your Applicant Status Portal. Simply log into your account, visit the Recommendations page, and update their contact details. From there, you can also resend invitation emails or add new recommenders if needed.
International Applicants
Expand All
Do I need a third-party evaluation (e.g., WES, ECE, SpanTran) if I attended school outside the United States?
Transcript evaluations are typically not required, however, Brandeis does reserve the right to require official transcripts or transcript evaluations at any time during the admission process. If a transcript evaluation is necessary, we will contact you directly and you will be asked to provide a course-by-course evaluation from an accredited evaluation company that currently holds membership to the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services (NACES).
My original academic documents are not in English. What is required for translation?
International applicants whose transcripts are not in English must have transcripts translated by a certified translation agency. Applicants may not translate their own transcripts.
How do I convert my GPA or marks to the U.S. 4.0 grading scale?
You should not attempt to convert your grades or GPA to the U.S. 4.0 scale. Brandeis admissions committees evaluate international transcripts within the context of your home institution's native grading system and country's educational framework. When completing your application, we ask that you report your GPA, cumulative percentage or grade marks exactly as they appear on your transcripts or mark sheets and provide the grading scales used by your university along with the official grading key/legend.
Do international applicants need to submit an English language proficiency score?
Learn more about the Graduate English Language Proficiency Requirements.
Do I need to submit financial proof (bank statements, affidavits) during the initial application?
No. Financial documentation is not required during the initial application process. If you are admitted and choose to enroll, you will work directly with our International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO) to submit your financial documents for the Visa Document Request Form (VIDOF) to obtain your visa sponsorship (I-20/DS-2019).
When and how do I apply for my I-20 or DS-2019 form?
You can apply for your Form I-20 (F-1 status) or Form DS-2019 (J-1 status) after you have formally accepted your offer of admission and paid your enrollment deposit. Once deposited, you will receive access to the ISSO Portal via your Brandeis email address. There, you will submit the Visa Information / Declaration of Finances (VIDOF) form along with a copy of your passport and required financial documentation.
I am an international applicant. Am I eligible for financial aid?
All admitted masters students, international or domestic, are considered for merit-based scholarships. Award types and amounts vary by program and degree type. Students are notified if they have received a scholarship in their admission decision letter.
Are graduate assistantships available to international students?
Yes. International graduate students at Brandeis University are eligible for graduate assistantships, such as Teaching Assistantships (TAs) and Research Assistantships (RAs), after completing at least one semester in their program. However, general hourly on-campus jobs are available for international students to apply for immediately upon starting their first semester.
What kind of support can I expect as a graduate student?
All graduate students receive academic guidance, student programming and support resources through the Office of Graduate Affairs. Additionally, international students are supported by the International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO). The ISSO provides guidance on immigration and visa status maintenance, advising on status-related topics (such as employment, academics and health insurance) and hosts dedicated events and newsletter updates throughout the year.
Can I defer my admission if my visa processing is delayed?
Admitted students may request a deferral of up to one year. Requests are evaluated on a case-by-case basis and are not guaranteed. To initiate a request, students must first submit their enrollment deposit, and financial aid/scholarship awards may be subject to re-evaluation for the deferred term.
